questions.stem: A hospital patient shows symptoms of confusion and swelling. Blood tests reveal high urea, high potassium, and excess water in the blood. Which organ system is most likely failing?

options.text: The digestive system, because it cannot absorb nutrients properly
The excretory system (kidneys), because they are not filtering waste and regulating blood composition
The respiratory system, because CO₂ is not being removed
The nervous system, because nerve impulses are disrupted

questions.explanation: High urea, high potassium, and excess water are all indicators of kidney failure. The kidneys normally filter urea, regulate ion concentrations, and control water balance. When they fail, these substances accumulate, causing the symptoms described.

questions.stem: A biology student creates a flow chart showing the journey of urea from production to excretion. Which sequence is correct?

options.text: Amino acids deaminated in kidneys → urea formed → excreted in urine
Amino acids deaminated in liver → ammonia converted to urea → urea travels in blood to kidneys → filtered out and excreted in urine
Proteins broken down in stomach → urea formed → excreted by lungs
Urea produced in muscles → transported to liver → excreted in bile

questions.explanation: Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver, producing ammonia which is quickly converted to less toxic urea. Urea dissolves in the blood and is transported to the kidneys, where it is filtered out during ultrafiltration and excreted in the urine.

questions.stem: On a cold day, a person notices they need to urinate more frequently than on a warm day, even though they have drunk the same amount of water. What explains this?

options.text: Cold temperatures cause the kidneys to filter blood faster
Less water is lost through sweating on cold days, so more water must be excreted by the kidneys to maintain water balance
ADH production increases on cold days, producing more dilute urine
The bladder contracts more in cold weather

questions.explanation: On cold days, we sweat less, so less water is lost through the skin. To maintain water balance, the kidneys must excrete the excess water, producing a larger volume of more dilute urine. This is regulated by reduced ADH secretion.

questions.stem: Which pair of organs work together to remove the waste products of protein metabolism from the body?

options.text: Lungs and heart
Liver and kidneys
Stomach and intestines
Pancreas and liver

questions.explanation: The liver deaminates excess amino acids and converts the toxic ammonia produced into urea. The kidneys then filter urea from the blood and excrete it in urine. Both organs are essential for the complete process of removing protein metabolism waste.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'The lungs are not excretory organs because they are part of the respiratory system.' Why is this statement incorrect?

options.text: Because the lungs excrete urea in exhaled air
Because the lungs excrete carbon dioxide and water vapour, which are metabolic waste products of respiration
Because the lungs absorb waste products from the blood
Because all organs in the body are excretory organs

questions.explanation: The lungs are indeed excretory organs because they remove CO₂ and water vapour — both waste products of aerobic respiration (a metabolic reaction). An organ can belong to more than one system; the lungs are involved in both gas exchange and excretion.
